title: Feijoada
subtitle: Brazilian black bean and pork stew
excerpt: Brazil's national dish: black beans slow-cooked with smoked pork sausage, pork ribs, and bacon until the beans are completely tender and the broth is thick, dark, and intensely smoky. Served with rice, oranges, collard greens, and farofa.

recipe.sourceNotes: Feijoada (from feijão, Portuguese for bean) is the national dish of Brazil, eaten throughout the country as a Saturday lunch tradition, typically served with white rice, sautéed collard greens (couve refogada), orange slices, farofa (toasted manioc flour), and hot pepper sauce. The dish has roots in the Portuguese cozido (a meat and bean stew) adapted in Brazil with the ingredients available: black beans rather than white, and a variety of pork cuts including parts traditionally discarded by the wealthy. Some food historians note that enslaved people on Brazilian plantations cooked the ears, trotters, and tails discarded by their enslavers with beans; others contest this origin story. The everyday version uses easily available smoked sausage, pork ribs, and bacon, which are the practical modern interpretation.

content.text: Use dried black beans soaked overnight for the best result; tinned beans work for a quicker version but will not give the same thick, starchy broth. The orange slices served alongside are not decoration: their acidity cuts through the richness of the pork and beans.

items.preparation: soaked overnight in cold water; drained

content.text: Heat the oil in a large pot over medium-high heat. Brown the pork ribs all over and remove. Fry the bacon until the fat renders. Add the onion and cook for 8 minutes until golden. Add the garlic and cook for 1 minute.

Return the ribs to the pot. Add the drained black beans and bay leaves. Cover with water by 4 cm. Bring to a boil, then reduce to a steady simmer. Cook covered for 1 hour. Add the chorizo and cook uncovered for a further 30 to 40 minutes until the beans are completely tender and the broth is thick and dark.

Remove 200 g of beans and mash roughly, then stir back in to thicken the stew. Season with salt and pepper. Remove the bay leaves. Serve with white rice, orange slices, sautéed collard greens, and hot sauce.
